---
title: "CLI Workflow"
description: "Run Revolte from a local repository when you want terminal context, command approval, and interactive build sessions."
---

<Note>
  <strong>Prerequisite</strong><br />
  You need an active workspace and application. Start with [Create Your First Feature](/docs/build/quick-start).
</Note>

The CLI workflow keeps Revolte close to the code. Use it when you are already working in a local repository and want the AI build session to share the same context as your terminal, tests, and branch.

## When to use the CLI

Use the CLI when:

- You want to run builds from a checked-out repository
- The task depends on local files or commands
- You need to iterate quickly on failing tests
- You want to inspect or approve actions step by step
- You prefer terminal workflows over dashboard workflows

## Install and authenticate

<Steps>
  <Step title="Install the CLI">
    ```bash
    npm install -g @revolte/cli
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Authenticate">
    ```bash
    revolte login
    ```

    This connects your local session to your Revolte workspace.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Start a build session">
    Run the session from the repository Revolte should inspect.

    ```bash
    revolte chat
    ```
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Start with a focused request

Describe one feature or fix at a time.

```txt
Add JWT authentication to the REST API, protect the user profile endpoint, and add tests for missing, invalid, and expired tokens.
```

Good CLI requests include:

- The behavior you want
- The affected area of the codebase
- Test expectations
- Constraints such as framework conventions or existing patterns
- Any known failure output if you are fixing a bug

## Approve actions

The CLI workflow is interactive. Revolte may propose file edits, commands, tests, or follow-up questions before completing the change.

Review each action for:

- File paths being changed
- Commands being executed
- Test scope
- Runtime or environment configuration updates
- Whether the change stays within the requested scope

> **Review before approving**  
> Approving a command or file edit should mean you understand why Revolte needs it for the current task.

## Resume a session

Use resume when a build spans multiple rounds of feedback or you need to refine an existing pull request.

```bash
revolte chat --continue <threadId>
```

## CLI workflow

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the repository">
    Navigate to the local repository for the application you want to change.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Start `revolte chat`">
    Revolte begins an interactive build session with repository context.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Describe the requirement">
    Provide the behavior, constraints, and validation expectations.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Review proposed actions">
    Inspect planned file edits, commands, and validation steps.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Approve implementation">
    Let Revolte modify code and run the checks required for the task.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Review the pull request">
    Confirm the generated output is correct before merging.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Best practices

- Start from a clean branch when possible.
- Keep each request focused on one feature or fix.
- Paste failing test output when debugging.
- Ask for tests for critical behavior.
- Review generated configuration changes carefully.
